cuisines.name: Mexican
cuisines.description: Corn, chillies and slow-cooked sauces, starting from the masa that holds it all together.

recipes.title: Nixtamal
recipes.yield: Fresh masa from 2 kg dried corn
recipes.description: Dried corn cooked and soaked in lime water, then washed and ground into fresh masa. This is the base for tortillas, tamales and sopes.

story.title: About this recipe
lines: Nixtamalization is the step that turns dried corn into masa. Cooking the kernels in lime water loosens their tough skins, lets the ground corn hold together as a dough, and makes the corn more nutritious.
White and blue corn are cooked together here, but you can make either one on its own. Halve the batch and keep the same method.

story.title: Make ahead & storage
lines: Once washed, nixtamal must be ground and used the same day. To keep it for 2–3 days, leave the unwashed corn in its nejayote and wash only what you need.

steps.text: Heat the {water} in a large stainless-steel or enamel pot. Once hot, add the {cal} and stir until it dissolves.
Add the {white corn} and {blue corn}, bring to the boil and cook for 40 minutes.
Take the pot off the heat and leave it uncovered to rest overnight, or for at least 8 hours.
Drain off the soaking liquid (the nejayote) and wash the corn well, rubbing off the loosened skins.
Grind the washed corn in a hand mill. Pass it through one, two or three times, until the dough is smooth enough to knead.
Knead briefly, then cover and set aside. The masa is now ready for other recipes.

notes: Use food-grade cal (calcium hydroxide, also sold as pickling lime). Quicklime (calcium oxide) is a different, caustic product, so don't substitute it.
Avoid aluminium pots: the alkaline water reacts with them.
